context.description: A refusal while a run is live answers in the session only (owner ruling 3)

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-VF2.spec.ts (2 tests, titles [VF2]); my own bun test run: 2 pass, 0 fail, 35 expect() calls. GIVEN a live run in a directory: a real /task job (jobs mode run) on a committed release-notes copy whose T1.1 and T1.2 wait on the outside T9; the real run supervisor, Recorder and status writer write status.json; the test polls until the decoded status is live (running or waiting, no ended tag, no endedAt, aliveAt set) and asserts the lease names the run. WHEN /task runs on a faulty spec in the same directory: a second spec folder (faulty.spec) with one planted R3 fault, run through the real TaskCommand.run with the same harness. THEN the session gets the refusal: the reply equals exactly the counted header, the R3 line and the hint, and is not the busy line; no new job starts. AND the status file still shows the live run: status.json decoded with TaskStatus.Status right after the refusal keeps the same state (waiting, not refused), spec, path, startedAt and task ids, has no reason, holds no faulty-spec text, and the lease still names the live run. A control proves the check discriminates: after the run is cancelled and the lease is free, the same refusal does write status.json as refused with the reason. The 5 s heartbeat makes an overwrite race in the read window unlikely. No gap found.
